classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange the sector-area formula separately for radius and angle, then recognise that the angle obtained in part (b) exceeds one full turn and cannot describe the stated ordinary sector.

content.prompt: Let the sector subtended by angle $\theta$ have area $625\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

spec.description: Unshaded narrow sector with centre above its curved boundary, two sloping radii labelled r, matching single perpendicular ticks and a central angle labelled θ. Opening is schematic and supplies no numerical angle.
spec.mathematics: Area is 625π cm²; θ and r are the variables. The original simple-sector figure conflicts with the givens in part (b).
spec.answerVisibility: Only r and θ are shown; no answers appear.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta\\625\pi&=\frac{1}{2}r^2\times\frac{\pi}{5}\\r^2&=6250\\r&=25\sqrt{10}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Take the positive square root because $r$ is a radius.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the value of $\theta$ if $r=8$ cm.

answer.short:
No ordinary sector satisfies these givens.

The formula gives $\theta=\frac{625\pi}{32}\text{ rad}>2\pi$, exceeding one full turn.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta\\625\pi&=\frac{1}{2}\times8^2\times\theta\\625\pi&=32\theta\\\theta&=\frac{625\pi}{32}\text{ rad}\end{align*}$$
This exceeds $2\pi$. A circle of radius $8$ cm has total area $64\pi\text{ cm}^2$, less than the given $625\pi\text{ cm}^2$, so the stated sector cannot exist.
